To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
five TFs belonging three different TF families (one TCP, one CPP and three NIN-Like TFs) are able to bind to OsNHX-1 promoter.
we have identified five novel TFs as potential regulators of the expression of the salt and drought induced OsNHX1.

we have identified five TFs binding to the promoter region of OsNHX in a rice genotype (Haswi) with a high salt tolerance, namely OsPCF2, a TCP; OsCPP5, a CPP; and three NIN like, OsNIN2-like, OsNIN3-like and OsNIN4-like.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of novel transcription factors binding to OsNHx1 promoter and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms regulating the expression of this gene in response to abiotic stress conditions.
a better understanding of OsNHX expression regulation in rice and the identification of TFs that can potentially be used to engineer plants with improved tolerance to salt stress.
the identification and characterization, in a rice genotype tolerant to salinity, of five TFs that are able to bind to the OsNHXI promoter and regulate its gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TFs identified in the present study are involved in the transcriptional activation or repression of OsNHX gene expression under abiotic stress conditions, particularly salt and drought stress.

the five TFs identified in this study may be involved in the regulation of the expression of OsNHX, but further studies are needed to elucidate the precise role of these TFs in the response to salt stress.

OsPCF, OsCPP and OsNIN-LIKE TFs play a role in the regulation of OsNHX gene expression in rice, however, the role of OsPCF and OsNIN- like TFs in the salt and PEG induced drought stress responses seems to be more important in a salt-tolerance rice genotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transcriptional regulation of OsNHX in response to salt and drought stress involves a complex mechanism that is not only dependent on TFs, but also on the plant genotype and the tissue under consideration.
the OsNHX gene expression regulation is complex, involving different TFs that act as transcriptional activator or repressor.
the OsNHX gene expression is regulated by different TFs, which may have different roles under salt or drought stress in rice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional regulation of OsNHX in rice is more complex than what we had previously thought.
the OsNHX expression is regulated by a set of five TFs belonging mainly to the TCP, CPP and NIN-like families.
OsNHX gene expression is regulated by different transcription factors, and the expression of these TFs is differentially regulated in a salt-tolerance rice genotype.
